GDTF channel footprint resolution

core/gdtf/gdtf_channel_footprint is the shared read-only address resolver for Viewer3D's public mode/channel API (including the fixture table's Ch Count) and the Core mode/channel browser. It resolves the selected mode's top-level geometry and each reference's unique top-level definition, then matches channel geometry names to actual elements within each instance, including descendants. The archive, geometry assignments, rendering and MVR data are not changed.

Following the GDTF 1.2 Geometry Type Reference and DMX Channel sections in the local specification, Break children are associated with the sorted distinct numeric source breaks of physical channels in that reference's subtree. An Overwrite channel uses the remaining Break entry. Each entry supplies the effective DMXBreak and DMXOffset (both default to 1). The physical address is the declared channel offset plus DMXOffset minus 1. Incomplete or ambiguous mappings produce diagnostics and no physical addresses for the affected channel instance.

Footprints are the highest occupied byte offset per effective break, including all declared coarse/fine/ultra/uber bytes and sparse addresses. Missing/None offsets are virtual and contribute no physical bytes. Addresses are integers, not DMXValues: an address above 255 is not an 8-bit value overflow.

The existing scalar channel-count API and browser's calculatedFootprint expose break 1 only, matching the existing single-address fixture table. They never sum separate breaks or take the maximum across unrelated breaks. The browser retains footprintsByBreak and each channel's effectiveDmxBreak; public channel rows retain dmxBreak. A multi-break mode generates a technical diagnostic. Displaying/editing all break footprints and addresses in the GUI remains a separate task; the single Ch Count column is not a complete multi-break summary.

For compatibility, files omitting DMXMode.Geometry retain direct channel addresses, with a diagnostic. Omitted channel geometry retains a direct address when the mode tree resolves. These are explicit legacy fallbacks, not claims of standard conformance.

Nested references and channel assignments targeting a GeometryReference node itself are not expanded. They produce diagnostics instead of guessed addresses. Missing definitions, non-top-level reference targets, duplicate/ambiguous names, cycles, malformed breaks/offsets and integer overflow likewise produce diagnostics. The browser retains unresolved channel source fields for inspection but exposes no calculated offsets; the legacy API logs the same diagnostics.

Regression tests generate description XML and temporary archives at runtime. They cover ordinary RGB, repeated referenced roots and child Beams (including 60 RGB pixels with exactly bytes 1–180), sparse and multibyte offsets, virtual channels, selected-tree scoping, independent breaks, Overwrite, the existing 16-byte GeometryExpanded case, invalid references and source preservation. This coverage does not establish full GDTF compatibility.
